title: A Echo for the Colony Anew
premise: Coral Reyes, a terraformer ferrying seed-stock along the silent corridor between the colonies of Meridian and Vesper, intercepts a distress call broadcast in Old Colonial — a language dead since the Severance two hundred years ago. The signal leads him to a hidden generation ship whose descendants still speak it, and whose existence is the secret both warring colonies would kill to bury. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down toward permanent silence, Coral must choose between delivering the ship's message of shared origin — which could end the war or ignite a genocide — and protecting the found family of linguists, deserters, and ship-born children who have taken him in. He delivers it, the truth of common ancestry shatters the war's justification, and the colonies' first joint fleet escorts the generation ship home as the loop ends on a message of peace instead of propaganda.
about_author: Yara Thackeray is a former agricultural scientist who spent a decade designing closed ecosystems before turning to fiction about worlds that refuse to be terraformed quietly. She writes from a converted greenhouse, where her novels and her tomatoes compete for light.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Establishing his solitary life ferrying seed-stock between Meridian and Vesper, two colonies that severed contact two centuries ago, and his tenderness for the unborn colonists his garden serves. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, cracked by the arrival of a distress signal in a language no living database recognizes.

chapters.title: Old Tongue, Old Wound
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Deciphering the signal with his ship's obsolete archive, Coral learns it's Old Colonial and traces it to the dead zone between colonies. His employer orders him to ignore it. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread as he realizes the signal predates the Severance — someone has been broadcasting for two hundred years.

chapters.title: The Ship That Waited
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He finds the generation ship Halcyon drifting in the dead zone, crewed by descendants of colonists abandoned when the Severance cut them off. A girl named Iyo, ship-born and fearless, greets him in Old Colonial. Beat: awe and guilt — the war's 'enemy' and 'traitor' are the same forgotten people.

chapters.title: What the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: POV alternating Coral/Iyo. Coral learns the Halcyon carries proof both colonies descend from one launched ark — the war's founding myth is a lie. Iyo teaches him the language; he teaches her the sky. Beat: found family taking root, and the first hint that Meridian's patrols have noticed his detours.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A Meridian patrol board his ship; Coral lies badly and barely escapes, now a fugitive on the route he once owned. His terraforming license is revoked, severing him from the garden and the unborn. Beat: the price of survival begins accruing — he has traded his future for the ship's past.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: POV Iyo. Earth's final transmission loop is revealed: in ninety days it ends forever, and with it the archive that could authenticate the Halcyon's proof. The ship's council splits — broadcast the truth and risk annihilation, or stay hidden and let the lie calcify. Beat: power's corruption shown in miniature, as the council's hawks seize the debate.

chapters.title: Deserter's Chorus
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He smuggles the Halcyon's linguist-elder, Sefa, toward Vesper's black-market archive, gathering a ragtag crew of deserters from both colonies along the way. Beat: warmth and banter amid danger — the found family completes itself — ending in ambush when a crew member's loyalty is bought.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The betrayer, Renn, reveals he sold them out not for money but because he believes the truth will trigger genocide against ship-descendants hiding in both colonies. Coral confronts him and, for the first time, doubts. Beat: the moral floor drops — delivering the message may be the cruelest act of all.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV alternating Coral/Iyo. With hours before the loop ends, Coral hijacks the transmission relay above Vesper while Iyo speaks the proof in Old Colonial on open channels to both worlds. Fleets converge; weapons arm. Beat: climax — the message goes out, and the war holds its breath as ancestry, not enemy, fills every screen.

chapters.title: A Echo for the Colony Anew
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In the silence after, the colonies waver, then stand down — the shared ark record is undeniable, and ship-descendants step out of hiding on both worlds. The first joint fleet escorts the Halcyon home as Earth's loop ends on Coral's relayed message of peace. Beat: resolution — Coral plants the garden's last seeds on the Halcyon, finally tending soil for people who exist.
